common_name: Rio Heuchera (Amber-to-Yellow Seasonal Color-Shift Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in moderately well-drained, organic soil; Rio is a vigorous Terra Nova selection grown for its unusually long seasonal color progression.

directions: Rio forms a large, vigorous mound of foliage that opens peach-amber and shifts through amber, tan, and finally a warm yellow-amber as the season progresses, giving the clump a different look from spring through fall. Short maroon flower spikes carry small white blooms from late spring into fall, drawing hummingbirds and other pollinators. Grow in moderately well-drained, humus-rich soil with average moisture, favoring the dry side once the clump is established. It holds its evergreen foliage well and suits mass plantings, mixed borders, and containers.

common_name: Topaz Jazz Heuchera (Honey-Gold-to-Lime Veiled Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in moderately well-drained, organic soil in part to full shade; best color develops with some direct morning light.

directions: Topaz Jazz carries a fast-growing mound of foliage that moves through honey-topaz, gold, and lime-green tones beneath a pale veiling overlay, creating a warm, shifting color effect across the season. Creamy yellow-green flowers rise on short maroon stems from midsummer into fall and attract hummingbirds. It prefers part to full shade but tolerates more sun than many heucheras if moisture is kept consistent, and it holds evergreen to semi-evergreen foliage through winter in milder zones. Use it as an accent, border edging, or container specimen in a shaded bed.

common_name: Little Cuties Shimmer Heuchera (Miniature Silver-Green Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in moderately well-drained, organic soil in part to full shade; avoid burying the crown.

directions: Shimmer is a dwarf-scale selection in Terra Nova's Little Cuties series, forming a tight mound of silver-green leaves well suited to troughs, rock garden pockets, and the front of a shaded border. It is noted as a freer-flowering, deeper-pink-blooming counterpart to the similarly sized 'Peppermint', sending up wiry stems of deep pink flowers over an unusually long season from spring into late fall. Grow in evenly moist, moderately well-drained soil in part to full shade, siting the crown at or slightly above grade to avoid rot. Its small size and long bloom window make it a useful miniature accent among larger shade perennials.
